acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients see a significant reduction in snoring intensity rather than complete elimination. The exact outcome depends on each patient's anatomy and contributing factors (weight, alcohol, sleep position, allergies). Many partners report a clearly quieter night even when snoring is not fully gone.

mainEntity.name: Is this a treatment for sleep apnea?

acceptedAnswer.text: NightLase is not a primary treatment for obstructive sleep apnea. If sleep apnea is suspected, we recommend a sleep study first and follow-up with a sleep specialist. NightLase can complement medical care in selected cases but does not replace CPAP or specialist evaluation.

There is a sensation of warmth in the back of the mouth and palate during the pulses. The session is performed without anaesthesia and most patients find it well tolerated. Normal eating and drinking resume right after.

hero.title: Fotona NightLase in Miami
hero.lede: NightLase is a non-invasive Fotona Nd:YAG laser protocol that gently heats the oral mucosa to tighten soft palate tissue and reduce snoring intensity over a short series of sessions.

blocks.title: What it does for you
list: Reduces snoring intensity by tightening the soft palate and surrounding oral tissue.
Non-invasive — no surgery, no anaesthesia, no devices to wear at night.
Each session lasts about 20–30 minutes; full protocol typically 3 sessions spaced 3 weeks apart.
Most patients and their partners report meaningful change after the third session.
Effect can be maintained with one session every 6 to 12 months.
Sleep apnea is evaluated separately — NightLase is not a substitute for medical sleep care.
